# LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming — facts

## Definitions

- [fact] For application-defined client tools, the model proposes a structured call and application code executes it, then returns the result in a subsequent request. LiteLLM's function-call example follows that loop; distinguish it from provider-hosted server tools that execute on provider infrastructure. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/function_call · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, LiteLLM, application, tool · also: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/tool-use/overview

## Structure and components

- [fact] With stream=True, consume LiteLLM's returned iterator; for asynchronous streaming, await acompletion and then async-iterate it. Text is carried in choices[].delta, so consumers must also handle structured tool deltas and terminal chunks instead of assuming every chunk contains text. — https://docs.litellm.ai/ · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, LiteLLM, acompletion, delta, stream, streaming · also: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/stream

## How it works

- [statement] SSE framing is UTF-8 text with events dispatched at blank lines, not one JSON document per network read. Its parser joins multiple data lines and ignores colon-prefixed comment lines; preserve that framing before interpreting provider-specific JSON payloads. — https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, JSON, SSE, UTF-8

## Parameters and configuration

- [fact] Request streaming usage deliberately. LiteLLM documents stream_options.include_usage; OpenAI's Chat Completions contract places total usage in a final chunk with choices=[] before [DONE], and an interrupted stream may omit it. Treat absent final usage as unknown, not zero. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/input · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, LiteLLM, [DONE], include_usage, stream, streaming · also: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] For OpenAI Chat Completions tool streams, accumulate argument fragments by the tool-call index. id, function.name and type may appear only in the first delta; preserve them while appending function.arguments, then parse the completed argument JSON. — https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, JSON, delta, function.arguments, index, stream
- [statement] LiteLLM exposes stream_chunk_builder to reconstruct a completed response from accumulated chunks. Its documented availability is not a substitute for checking preservation of tool IDs, argument JSON, finish reasons and provider-specific metadata in the selected streaming path. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/stream · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, JSON, LiteLLM, stream_chunk_builder, streaming, tool
- [fact] Validate function.arguments as JSON and against the expected tool schema before execution. LiteLLM's example warns about invalid JSON, and OpenAI's API reference warns about invalid JSON or invented arguments; a successful completion response is not a validated invocation. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/function_call · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, JSON, LiteLLM, function.arguments, tool · also: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create
- [fact] For OpenAI-style Chat Completions, append the original assistant tool-call message, then append a role=tool result with the matching tool_call_id for each returned call before requesting the next completion. Do not reduce this conversation state to message.content alone. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/function_call · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, tool, tool-call, tool_call_id · also: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling
- [fact] Use supports_function_calling and supports_parallel_function_calling as capability checks for the exact model/provider. The inspected helpers read model metadata; they do not execute a tool round trip, so qualify the actual deployment before enabling an autonomous tool loop. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/function_call · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, supports_function_calling, supports_parallel_function_calling, tool · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/82d8b3797cf124e2baaa9c342f87a57fbb3a1a96/litellm/utils.py

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [fact] LiteLLM's inspected repetition guard tracks consecutive identical text deltas longer than two characters and raises InternalServerError at REPEATED_STREAMING_CHUNK_LIMIT. This text-repetition safeguard does not replace explicit request timeouts or output-token limits. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/stream · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, InternalServerError, LiteLLM, REPEATED_STREAMING_CHUNK_LIMIT, delta · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/82d8b3797cf124e2baaa9c342f87a57fbb3a1a96/litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py
- [fact] Handle errors during both stream creation and consumption. LiteLLM's exception example encloses iteration in its handler, and Anthropic documents error events inside an established SSE stream; successful headers alone do not establish successful completion. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/exception_mapping · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, LiteLLM, SSE, stream · also: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming

## Changes and history

- [statement] An upstream report for LiteLLM 1.98.0-rc.1 with a vLLM Chat Completions backend describes tool-argument deltas arriving in an end-of-stream burst when include_usage=true. The report was still open at inspection; it was not reproduced here and does not establish a defect in every version or provider. — https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/38926 · keywords: LiteLLM tool calls and SSE streaming, LiteLLM, delta, include_usage
